title: High-fidelity and robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. II. System-parameter uncertainties and overall errors
abstract: In the companion paper (Part I), we developed an optimal-control framework to suppress intrinsic and decoherence-induced errors in controlled-Z (CZ) gates between directly coupled, frequency-tunable transmons. Here, we extend this framework to incorporate uncertainties in coupling strength, anharmonicities, and zero-flux qubit frequencies, enabling the design of high-fidelity gates robust against noise and parameter uncertainties. We classify these uncertainties by whether they perturb the off-diagonal coupling strengths or the diagonal detunings of the Hamiltonian, and we identify distinct suppression mechanisms for each class. Coupling errors are mitigated through dynamical decoupling induced by strong detuning modulation. For a 30-ns gate, this strategy reduces the coupling error to $6.21\times10^{-7}$ and tolerates coupling-strength uncertainties up to $2π\times4$ MHz while keeping total gate infidelity below $10^{-3}$. Detuning errors are minimized near a symmetric-detuning operating point that balances the two dominant leakage-mediated interactions. A 24-ns gate operated near this point tolerates individual uncertainties of up to $2π\times5$ MHz in each relevant diagonal parameter under the same infidelity threshold. We further optimize gate performance under realistic conditions where intrinsic errors, decoherence, and parameter uncertainties coexist across six representative stages of progressively improving hardware performance. The resulting stage-specific controls achieve lower infidelity and greater robustness. Together with the companion study (Part I), this framework offers a practical approach to balance speed, fidelity, and robustness while reducing the need for exhaustive characterization and frequent recalibration in large-scale superconducting quantum processors.
summary: This paper presents an advanced optimal control framework to design highly robust controlled-Z gates for superconducting transmon qubits. It tackles the challenge of system-parameter uncertainties by implementing distinct error suppression techniques for coupling and detuning errors. The resulting methods offer a practical path to achieving high fidelity gates that are less sensitive to hardware imperfections and require less frequent recalibration.
main_problem: The paper addresses the critical challenge of designing controlled-Z (CZ) gates for superconducting transmon qubits that maintain high fidelity despite inherent system-parameter uncertainties and environmental noise.
main_result: The authors developed a framework combining dynamical decoupling for coupling errors and operating near a symmetric-detuning point for detuning errors, achieving gate fidelities below $10^{-3}$ while tolerating significant parameter variations.
method: The methodology extends optimal control theory to incorporate parameter uncertainty Hamiltonians, classifying errors into off-diagonal (coupling) and diagonal (detuning) perturbations, and deriving specific suppression mechanisms for each.
model_or_system: The physical system is superconducting transmon qubits. The analysis involves modeling the CZ gate operation and quantifying errors arising from uncertainties in coupling strength, anharmonicities, and qubit frequencies within the Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Gate infidelity (target $< 10^{-3}$), coupling error reduction ($6.21 	imes 10^{-7}$ for 30-ns gate), and tolerance to parameter uncertainties (e.g., $2\pi 	imes 4$ MHz for coupling).
important_parameters: Gate duration (e.g., 24-ns, 30-ns), uncertainty magnitudes ($ eta_{gAB}, \sigma_\delta$), and the operating regime near the symmetric-detuning point.
main_assumptions: Assumptions include treating uncertainties as normally distributed with zero mean, and using approximations based on the strong coupling limit for error derivations.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates how robust control expands the parameter space region of low infidelity, while Figure 2 compares error contributions for optimized CZ gates at specific durations.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon a companion study (Part I) by systematically incorporating parameter uncertainties. It analyzes coupling and detuning errors separately, deriving specific suppression techniques (dynamical decoupling vs. symmetric-detuning point), and finally optimizes performance across multiple hardware improvement stages.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it provides actionable, quantitative guidelines for building fault-tolerant quantum hardware by explicitly managing parameter uncertainty, a major bottleneck in scaling superconducting quantum processors.
